1.explanation:
The ContentSwitcher class is where the `light` prop must be declared and handled. We need to extend its static `propTypes` to include a boolean `light` prop, add `light: false` to `defaultProps`, and update the `render` method’s `classNames` call to conditionally apply the `
`${prefix}--content-switcher--light`
` modifier when `light` is true. Additionally, the component’s core configuration file (content-switcher.config.js) defines Storybook variants—so we must add a new `light` variant there (context: { light: true }) so docs and demos reflect the new theme option.
1.bug_scenario: The bug shows the ContentSwitcher rendered on a dark (ui-01) page background: the selected switch button blends into the white page area and the unselected button has insufficient contrast, making the controls hard to read. We need to add a `light` variant/prop so that, when used on dark backgrounds, the switcher applies a light theme class (e.g. `--content-switcher--light`) to invert its colors.

2.explanation:
1. content-switcher.config.js: This config file defines the variants for the vanilla JS component. A new “light” variant (with context.light = true and the appropriate notes) must be added here so designers can preview it.
2. ContentSwitcher.js (class ContentSwitcher): This React class doesn’t yet accept or act on a `light` prop. We need to add `light: PropTypes.bool` and `light: false` in defaultProps, then update the render() method’s classNames call to include `${prefix}--content-switcher--light` when `this.props.light` is true.
3. ContentSwitcher-story.js (function contentSwitcher): The Storybook story generator for ContentSwitcher needs a new boolean knob for the `light` prop and must pass it into the rendered component so engineers can QA the light variant.
4. ContentSwitcher-test.js: The unit tests must be extended to assert that when `<ContentSwitcher light>…</ContentSwitcher>` is rendered, the container has the `--light` modifier class, preventing regressions.
2.bug_scenario: The ContentSwitcher component currently renders white-on-white styling when placed on a dark “ui-01” background, making the active switch indistinguishable. In the provided screenshot, the switch labeled “By reviewer” blends into the white track and fails to contrast against the dark page background. A light variant (similar to TextInput’s “--light” mode) is needed so the switches render in an inverted (dark-on-light) style when placed on dark backgrounds.
